cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Basically Finished
cards.instruction: Describe incomplete, late, or improvised work as a thoughtful version of completion.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Finished. I've left the cupboard shelves loose so you can practise the measuring I taught you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They fall down. There aren't any supports.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're finally checking underneath. It's a complete practice kit; you choose the heights around your tins.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I paid you to install it, not set homework. Here's the drill.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll finish one shelf for you to copy. A complete demonstration, with room for you to show what you learned.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 loose shelves are completed measuring practice; A3 grades B2 inspection and calls absence of supports a complete kit; A5 responds to B4 paid-duty objection with a complete demonstration rather than installation.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 falling shelves causes A3 kit reinterpretation; B4 drill and payment causes A5 promise of one fitted model.

relationship.evidence: B4 identifies the actual contractual task and supplies the needed tool, resisting the invented homework purpose.

heightening.evidence: A5 makes a small genuine concession while renaming it completion of a different teaching deliverable.

specificity.evidence: A1 cupboard shelves and B2 supports make actual unfinished work clear.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 room-to-show-learning gives the pupil a purported benefit for the missing remaining work.
